b: Running from Apr to Jul 2027, the JASANZ Futures x Responsible Wood programme will help forestry businesses develop in-house auditing expertise while creating a pathway for experienced auditors from other sectors to enter forestry.

From left: Richard Laity (PEFC International), Simon Bannock (JASANZ), Simon Dorries (former Responsible Wood CEO), who was instrumental in the programme’s early planning and development, and Graeme Benny (JASANZ)

A new training programme aims to strengthen auditing capability across the forestry sectors in Australia and New Zealand, equipping businesses with the skills to navigate certification requirements and ensuring a wider pool of specialists can assess forest management practices against certification standards.
Known as the JASANZ Futures x Responsible Wood programme, the initiative will also give auditors already working in the forestry sector an opportunity to upskill.

To encourage industry participation, Responsible Wood, the national governing body for the Programme for the Endorsement of Forest Certification (PEFC) in Australia and New Zealand, is sponsoring 15 places on the programme.
“Forest certification gives businesses a credible way to demonstrate responsible forest management and meet market expectations,” said Responsible Wood acting CEO Matt de Jongh.

“By investing in auditing capability, our goal is to continue reinforcing the integrity of sustainable forest management practices, to equip businesses with additional skills to maintain their certification and to ensure forests are responsibly managed for generations to come,” he said.

PEFC International’s Richard Laity (top right) meets with JASANZ’s Simon Bannock (top left), Caroline Bell-Singh (bottom left), Tatiana Bridova (bottom right) and technical consultant Kevin Reardon (on screen) during a programme planning session in Wellington

The programme combines Responsible Wood’s expertise in sustainable forest management certification with JASANZ’s expertise in accreditation and conformity assessment. Training will include online learning, mentoring and field trip opportunities, and is recognised by PEFC as initial training for forest management auditors.
JASANZ CEO Sarah Valentine said the partnership represented an investment in market confidence.

“Accredited certification is part of the infrastructure of trade. It gives businesses a way to show their products and practices meet the standards their markets expect. Our partnership with Responsible Wood is a long-term commitment to forestry and the trade it supports,” she said.
With PEFC certification adoption growing in New Zealand, the programme also presents an opportunity to strengthen auditing capability across the trans-Tasman forestry sector.

“The programme builds on existing capability in the region, complementing sustainable forestry practices with on-the-ground support from JASANZ technical assessors alongside PEFC New Zealand,” said PEFC International’s South Pacific programme manager, Richard Laity.
“While the programme was designed for Australian and New Zealand audiences, it remains open to forestry and conformity assessment professionals from other regions,” he added.
The programme will run from Apr to Jul 2027, with sessions delivered by specialists from Responsible Wood, JASANZ and PEFC.
